objectives: Hear and identify short /o/ in simple spoken words.
Discriminate short /o/ from previously taught short /a/, /i/ and /u/ sounds.
Connect short /o/ to the grapheme o.
Identify short /o/ in initial teaching examples without requiring independent decoding yet.
concepts: Short vowels are identified by their sounds in words.
The middle vowel is critical in CVC word discrimination.
Auditory discrimination should precede independent decoding of a new vowel pattern.

definitions.definition: The short vowel sound represented by o in taught CVC words such as hot and mop.
The smallest sound unit in a spoken word.
A letter or group of letters used to represent a sound.

workedExamples: mop → identify /o/ and connect it to o.
hot versus hat → listen for the changed middle vowel.
commonMistakes: Naming the letter without attending to its sound.
Focusing on the first or final consonant instead of the middle vowel.
revisionPoints: short /o/ → o → middle vowel in CVC words.

application: Connect /o/ to o in taught examples.
higherOrderThinking: Explain which sound changes in a minimal pair.
mixedReview: Discriminate short /o/ from previously taught short vowels.

weakTopicRevision: Repeat auditory minimal pairs before adding new decoding demands.

outcomes: Learner identifies short /o/ in taught spoken examples with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner distinguishes short /o/ from short /a/ and /i/ in minimal contrasts.
Learner connects short /o/ with the grapheme o with at least 90% accuracy.
Learner identifies the middle vowel as the key contrast in CVC words.
